title: Escalation + Support SLA policy refresh (tiered targets, approvals, rollout)
creator: Dev Patel
project: CS & Support Escalation Playbook Refresh + Known-Issues Sprint (Feb 2026)
description: Define and publish a single tiered Support SLA policy (response + update cadence + escalation triggers) for Hosted API / Dedicated / Private, aligned to Engineering on-call practices and contract language. Includes approval path (CS + Legal + Eng/SRE) and rollout plan (internal training + Confluence + docs-site links + Jira automation).
acceptance_criteria: SLA policy table finalized for tiers: self_serve, dedicated, private, enterprise (definitions + coverage windows).
Support Priority (P0–P4) language consistent with severity mapping (Sev0–Sev3) and escalation triggers.
Policy explicitly states: first response target, update cadence while investigating, and escalation thresholds to page Eng/SRE.
Clear after-hours policy (what is covered, what is best-effort) and ‘Waiting on Customer’ handling that does not create SLA confusion.
Credits / contract exception guidance included with explicit approval requirements and what Support can/can’t promise.
Approvals captured from CS leadership (Jasmine Liu, Rachel Kim), SRE (Sean Gallagher or Rafael Mendes), Legal (Sofia Mendes).
Rollout plan completed: Confluence pages published, Support macros updated, Jira SLA timers/reminders configured, internal announcement sent.
proposed_policy_summary: This refresh standardizes Support SLAs across deployment tiers and ties escalation triggers to measurable customer impact. The policy is written for Support to execute consistently (Jira + Slack) and for Engineering/SRE to trust (pages only when warranted, includes required context). Contract language is preserved: SLAs are ‘support response SLAs’ (not availability SLOs), with clear coverage windows and update cadence expectations for enterprise accounts during active incidents.
policy_details_working_draft:
Tiers and coverage:
- self_serve (Hosted API, no contract): business-hours coverage; best-effort after-hours for platform-wide incidents.
- dedicated (reserved capacity): 24x5 standard, 24x7 optional for premium SLA (note: contract-dependent).
- private (VPC/on-prem): 24x5 standard, 24x7 optional for premium SLA; strict change-window and customer-owned infra considerations called out.
- enterprise (contracted, may be Hosted/Dedicated/Private): SLA terms governed by MSA/SOW; this doc defines default internal targets + comms cadence.

Targets (default internal targets; do not paste into contracts):
- P0 (customer production outage / broad severe degradation): first response <= 15 min (24x7 for enterprise with premium coverage; otherwise next coverage window + immediate status-page alignment if platform-wide). Updates every 30–60 min while actively mitigating.
- P1 (major degradation, workaround exists, or single high-revenue customer impacted): first response <= 1 hour; updates every 2–4 hours (or per enterprise expectation during active incident).
- P2 (limited impact / non-urgent degradation): first response same business day; daily updates while investigating.
- P3/P4 (how-to, minor issues, feature requests): response in 1–2 business days; updates weekly or when status changes.

Escalation triggers (page Eng/SRE):
- Any credible P0: page immediately with required context (request IDs, region, model/version, start time, customer tier, error rate/latency symptoms, known-issue check).
- P1 becomes page-worthy if: multiple customers impacted, repeatable across regions, suspected regression after deploy, or customer has contractual uptime commitments / exec attention.
- Never page for ‘needs info’ tickets; collect minimum diagnostic set first (unless widespread incident is clearly underway).

‘Waiting on Customer’ handling:
- SLA timers pause only when Support has explicitly requested specific artifacts and the customer acknowledged; update cadence still applies for enterprise when impact is ongoing (status: ‘pending customer’ but with scheduled check-ins).

Credits and exceptions:
- Support does not commit credits. Credits requests require CS Lead approval (Rachel Kim) + Sales owner alignment; executive escalations require Jasmine Liu approval. If tied to platform-wide incident, follow status page + incident comms alignment doc and decision log expectations.

Comms alignment:
- For platform-wide incidents: use #incidents channel, status page decision flow, and keep Support emails consistent with incident lead updates. For single-account issues: Support owns customer comms, Engineering provides mitigation statement; do not speculate on root cause before confirmation.
links: Internal tasks: INT-333 (Jira automation), INT-332 (Slack bridge workflow)
approval_plan:
Required sign-offs (in order):
1) CS/Support: Jasmine Liu (exec sponsor), Rachel Kim (enterprise CS) to confirm customer-facing expectations and coverage.
2) Eng/SRE: Sean Gallagher or Rafael Mendes to confirm paging thresholds and that update cadence is operationally feasible during incidents.
3) Legal: Sofia Mendes to confirm no conflict with MSA/SOW language; ensure doc is clearly labeled as internal policy + does not create new contractual commitments.
4) Product Ops: Chris Osei to confirm tier definitions match packaging and Sales enablement guidance.

Artifact control: publish to Confluence under Customer Success & Support > Escalation Playbook. Mark as ‘Internal’ and avoid customer-specific examples. Templates that can be forwarded to customers must be in the comms templates page with vetted language.
rollout_plan:
Week plan (2-week sprint + follow-up):
- Planning week:
  - Align on tier definitions + coverage windows with CS/Support.
  - Review SRE feedback and adjust paging triggers to match SLO alerting.
  - Draft policy page + add examples for P0/P1 boundaries.
- Execution week:
  - Publish Confluence page.
  - Update Support macros/snippets to reference SLA targets + required context.
  - Jira automation: enforce required fields at triage, start SLA timers, reminders for update cadence, prompt known-issues index linking.
  - Slack bridge workflow: template post includes SLA tier + priority + next update time.
- Follow-up week:
  - Train Support (30-min live + quick reference) and confirm adoption.
  - Audit first 10 escalations for compliance (fields filled, cadence met, correct paging).
  - Share early metrics and gaps; open follow-up tasks as needed.
metrics_and_success_criteria:
Primary success metrics (measure over 2–4 weeks post-rollout):
- Time-to-triage (median) for P0/P1 tickets down 20%.
- Time-to-first-engagement for paged incidents down (page includes correct context; fewer back-and-forth).
- SLA compliance: % first response met by tier/priority; % updates posted on schedule for enterprise P0/P1.
- Repeat ticket rate reduction for top known-issues categories (streaming disconnects, 429 confusion, autoscaling oscillation, audit log lag).

Operational guardrails:
- Reduce ‘unnecessary pages’ (pages lacking request IDs/region/model) by enforcing intake checklist + Slack template.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risks:
- Over-promising in internal docs that Sales/CS forwards to customers.
- Misalignment between Support update cadence and Engineering incident bandwidth.
- Confusion between Support SLAs (response) and Engineering SLOs (availability/latency).

Mitigations:
- Explicit labeling: internal targets; contracts control external commitments.
- Tie paging triggers to customer impact thresholds and require minimum diagnostic context.
- Add a short ‘SLA vs SLO’ explainer section with examples; link to SRE mapping doc.
open_questions: Confirm default coverage windows for Dedicated and Private customers without premium add-on (24x5 vs 24x7 best-effort).
Decide whether enterprise P0 updates are ‘every 30 min’ or ‘every 60 min’ as default (SRE prefers flexibility based on incident phase).
Define whether SLA timers pause automatically in Jira when status = Waiting on Customer, and what qualifies as a pause-worthy request.
Clarify policy for customer-requested comms channels (shared Slack vs email) and how cadence is tracked.
latest_status_update: 2026-02-15: Draft policy language incorporated SRE feedback (avoid hard-coding 30-min updates in all cases; use 30–60 min during active mitigation, 60–120 min during monitoring). Tier definitions aligned with Product Ops notes; still pending Legal sign-off on the ‘internal targets’ disclaimer block. Rollout tasks (INT-333/INT-332) are in progress; docs/Confluence publication queued once approvals complete.
commentary: 2026-02-06 (Sean Gallagher): Update cadence needs to reflect incident phase; paging trigger should not be tied solely to ‘enterprise customer asks’—must be tied to observable impact or credible regression. Also: be explicit that Support SLA != availability SLO.

2026-02-07 (Rachel Kim): Enterprise expectations: acknowledge fast, then commit to a next update time even if we have no new info. ‘Waiting on Customer’ needs a standard sentence and a scheduled follow-up time to avoid perceived abandonment.

2026-02-09 (Priya Natarajan): Platform ownership boundaries need to be reflected in escalation triggers (SSO/audit logs/quota are Platform first; runtime performance regressions involve Runtime on-call + SRE for incident mgmt).

2026-02-11 (Sofia Mendes): Ensure the policy cannot be construed as amending contractual SLAs. Add a prominent disclaimer and avoid using ‘guarantee’ language. Credits language must state approvals and avoid promises.

2026-02-14 (Jasmine Liu): Approved approach contingent on rollout readiness (macros + Jira automation) so Support can actually meet cadence. Wants a quick reference table for Support and a separate deeper policy page for audits.
